newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-COWBOYS STARS' ACCUSER CHARGED FOR "MALICIOUS" LIES.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-COWBOYS STARS' ACCUSER CHARGED FOR "MALICIOUS" LIES.

text.p: A woman who falsely accused Dallas Cowboys stars Michael Irvin and Erik Williams of sexually assaulting her at gunpoint was herself charged on Tuesday for making the "malicious" allegations, police said.
Sgt. Jim Chandler said Nina Shahravan, 23, was formally charged with filing a false police report, a misdemeanour offence, and would face up to six months in jail and a $2,000 fine if convicted.
Shahravan had accused Irvin of holding a gun to her head and threatening to kill her while Williams and a third man raped her on a pool table inside Williams' home on Dec. 29.
But she recanted her story last Friday after police confronted her with the evidence gathered during an 11-day investigation.

"Based on our investigation, Shahravan made malicious and false criminal allegations of sexual assault against three men. She will be charged with the appropriate statute for her actions," the Dallas Police Department said in a statement.
Irvin's attorney, Royce West, quickly supported the police action. "She's a pathological liar," he said of the former topless dancer.
Chandler said Shahravan had 24 hours to turn herself in or pay a $500 bond, and that she would be arrested if she does not.
Her allegations came days before the Cowboys, who have won three Super Bowls in the last four years, were eliminated from this year's title hunt by the Carolina Panthers.

Irvin, 30, and Williams, 28, are All-Pro stars who have played a key role in the Cowboys' success in the 1990s. Irvin is one of the NFL's premier wide receivers and Williams a standout offensive lineman. Both have been in trouble with the law in the past.

Irvin is currently on four years probation after pleading no contest to felony cocaine possession charges last year. He was arrested after being found in a motel room with a former teammate and two strippers, as well as drugs and sex toys.
If Irvin had been arrested on aggravated sexual assault charges, he could have had his probation revoked and been sent to jail.
Williams was in 1995 accused of sexually assaulting a 17-year-old topless dancer but a grand jury declined to indict him after he reached a settlement with the woman.
Both players insisted from the start that Shahravan's allegations were false and police said last Friday that the players had told the truth.
Shahravan's accusations had sparked a wave of published attacks on the Cowboys team, which has been rocked by a string of drugs and sex scandals in the last two years.
